name: Average Teaching Dimension of Blockwise-Addressing
proof: Each $f_i$ is taught by $(z,0),(x_i,1)$ and each $g_i$ by $(z,1),(y_i,1)$.  No one-coordinate sample identifies any member of either family: at $z$ it leaves all members of that family, at a private coordinate it agrees with a member of the opposite family, and at a block coordinate its label occurs for multiple members of the same family.  Thus every individual minimum teaching-set size is two, and their average is two.
